# Draft:Greek Independence Day Parade (Boston)

----
Greek Independence Day Parade (Boston) is an annual parade held in Boston, Massachusetts, United States, celebrating Greek Independence Day. The event is organized by Greek-American organizations in the New England region and typically takes place along Boylston Street in Boston's Back Bay neighborhood. It is considered one of the most visible celebrations of Greek heritage in the region and one of the principal public events of the Greek-American community in Boston, attracting participants from across the Greek diaspora in the northeastern United States.
History
The parade commemorates the anniversary of the start of the Greek War of Independence in 1821. Over the years it has developed into a major cultural event for the Greek-American community in New England.
The event has been held annually for several decades and features participation from cultural associations, Greek schools, community organizations, and church groups.
After a pause during the COVID-19 pandemic, the parade resumed with strong participation from the Greek-American community and attendance from public officials and representatives of Greek organizations.
Route
The parade is traditionally held in the Back Bay neighborhood of Boston and proceeds along Boylston Street, one of the city's central avenues. The route passes through areas of the city frequently used for civic celebrations and public gatherings.
Organization
The parade is organized by Greek-American community organizations in the Boston area, including the Federation of Hellenic American Societies of New England (FHASNE). The event is supported by cultural associations, churches, and community groups representing the Greek diaspora across New England.
Participation
Participants in the parade typically include:
* Greek cultural associations
* Greek language schools
* Hellenic student groups
* church communities
* diaspora organizations from across New England
The event often features traditional Greek music, cultural performances, and marching groups representing different segments of the Greek-American community.
Attendance
The parade attracts participants and spectators from across the New England region. Community members, local officials, and representatives of Greek-American organizations regularly attend the event as part of the wider celebrations of Greek Independence Day.
